config.name: PROOF / REPS
config.hypothesis: Will gym-goers explore the products, add an item to the bag and finish the simulated checkout? Learn which payment method they would prefer and what would prevent a real purchase.

questions.label: If this were a real purchase, which checkout method would you prefer?
What would be most likely to stop you from buying?

options.label: I would need more trust or clarity in checkout
I would need more sizing or fit information
The products were not compelling enough
I was only testing the demo

questions.label: What would make you more likely to buy from this store?

limitations: page_view is already collected automatically and is not repeated here; it can provide top-of-funnel traffic but not product-level exploration detail.
collection_nav_clicked undercounts exploration because visitors can scroll directly to the products without using the navigation link.
bag_button_clicked is a click-level signal from the bag button attribute hook; it should be interpreted as intent to inspect the bag, not as guaranteed modal visibility in every edge case.
demo_checkout_completed measures only a successful simulated checkout. It does not represent a wallet connection, payment, shipment, or verified sale.
There is no dedicated event for product card viewing or size selection, so product exploration is only approximated through navigation and add-to-bag behavior.
If testers use browser automation or developer tools outside the visible UI patterns, results may not perfectly reflect ordinary shopper behavior.

nextSteps: Use these records to verify tracking and feedback delivery. Internal tests and agent activity do not establish customer demand.
Collect candid feedback from intended users before making product decisions.
limitations: Primary actions indicate interaction, not verified sales or completed outcomes.
Action occurrences count accepted unique event IDs; retrying an ID does not add an action. Earlier session-only records cannot recover repeat counts.
The selected period includes sessions started since midnight UTC at its beginning. A session lasts up to 24 hours.
Funnel counts require all preceding events in a session; they do not establish chronological order or explain why someone stopped.
Sessions are opted-in browser visits, not verified unique people.
Audience labels and feedback are self-reported; this is not proof of human identity.
Records expire after 90 days. AWS metrics include assets, bots, owner visits and authentication failures.
